text:
Rina: Quick PSA — found a YAML file that reads like modern art: `version: v3...0` and a tab-indented list of feelings. :art: :sweat_smile:
Ben: wait. v3...0? that's not a bug, that's performance art.
Rina: right? parser output was: 
Rina: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/parser.py", line 42, in load
    raise YAMLError('Unexpected token')
YAMLError: Unexpected token '.' at line 1
```
ci-bot: Build failed: SemverViolation - version 'v3...0' does not match '^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$'
Theo: imagine explaining to product that release got delayed because yaml had an existential crisis. :man_shrugging:
Ben: can we make the linter louder? like, needs a haiku and a clown horn before merge.
Rina: haiku-linter sounds expensive but also emotionally responsible.
Theo: proposed quick fix: pre-commit hook that auto-corrects 2+ consecutive dots -> single dot and pads missing patch to .0. also convert tabs -> two spaces.
ci-bot: Suggested fix applied: Replace 'v3...0' -> 'v3.0.0' ; Tabs replaced with two spaces. Automated commit: https://ci.internal/auto/3344
Ben: commit message suggestion: "Save YAML from itself (feat: semver therapy)" :laughing:
Rina: also added a small note in README: "If your version looks like Morse code, please consult a human."
Theo: i'm in favor of stickers: "I fixed semver and all I got was this YAML."
Ben: bonus sticker for anyone who actually writes a semver haiku in commit message.
Rina: challenge accepted. placing a small bounty: 1 coffee for best semver haiku.
ci-bot: Pipeline rerun succeeded  staging deployed :rocket:
Theo: glory. time to go worship at the altar of two-space indentation.
